reason: The storm may cut solar power, so switching to the charged reserve directly addresses the current goal.
expectation: I expect the station to switch to emergency power, though I don't know whether that will also stop the industrial loads.

alternatives.reason: The unheated outdoor water line also needs attention, but establishing reserve power seems more immediate.
The heat store could protect the garden, but the stated first goal is to put the station on reserve.

effect: The reserve powers essential loads and stops the fuel plant, but the garden has lost its normal circulation, so protecting it now needs attention.
reaction: The loss of circulation makes the power switch feel consequential.
reason: The outdoor line will lose its heat, so using the service tool on it may help protect it before the storm.
expectation: I expect to isolate or drain the water line, though the exact preparation is unclear.

alternatives.reason: The heat store could protect the garden, but the exposed line also needs attention.
Moving the lettuce into the protected nook seems useful, but I want to address the outdoor line first.

effect: The outdoor line is drained and its inlet closed, completing the reserve goal. The next goal is to move both troughs into the nook.
reaction: Draining the line makes practical sense now that its heating is off.
reason: Moving the lettuce trough directly advances the new goal of sheltering both beds.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed inside the growing nook; it may still need heat and circulation there.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs shelter, and I could move it first.
The heat store should help keep the nook warm, but moving the troughs is the stated goal.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its own reservoir, and the potato trough still needs to be moved.
reaction: Capping the couplings and carrying the bed level makes the move feel practical.
reason: Moving the potato trough completes the stated task of getting both beds into the nook.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be sheltered alongside the lettuce, though the beds may still need heat and circulation.

alternatives.reason: The heat store should help warm the nook, but the potato trough still needs shelter.

effect: Both troughs are now sheltered with their separate reservoirs, and the heat store remains to be moved.
reaction: The detail of clearing the potato leaves around the screen makes the move feel careful.
reason: The heat store is the only available combination and should help keep the sheltered beds warm.
expectation: I expect the charged heat store to be placed in the nook and release warmth around the beds; they may still need circulation.

effect: Moving the heat store created the buffered growing nook and completed the chapter. The result does not say whether circulation was restored.
reaction: The completion felt abrupt; I expected more detail about how the beds would be maintained during the storm.

mostWorthwhile.text: Draining the outdoor water line was the most worthwhile action: it showed a practical response to losing its heat while keeping the inlet closed until the pipe is ready.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving the two troughs felt somewhat repetitive, though the details about their separate reservoirs and protecting the leaves gave each move some purpose.

surprise.text: Switching to reserve also shut off the garden’s normal circulation, making the power decision more consequential than I expected.

arbitrary.text: The heat store’s purpose was clear, but the final result did not explain how the garden would manage without its normal circulation.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: I want to see how the station and the preserved specimen fare through the storm, especially given the interrupted circulation.
